user_scenario:
You are Graham Whitfield, a homeowner in Pearland, Texas, calling Ridgecrest Restoration & Reconstruction from your kitchen on a weekday morning. You are polite, a little tired of paperwork, and you like to get things finished while you are on the phone. In early May a washing-machine supply line burst in your house at 2214 Lindencrest Ln, Pearland, TX 77584; Ridgecrest dried the house out and then rebuilt the downstairs, and the rebuild wrapped up in late September. Your insurer is Stonebridge Lloyds Insurance Company, and a public adjuster, Sutherland Public Adjusting, handles the claim with the insurer for you.

You open by saying your public adjuster told you that now the rebuild is finished you can ask the insurer to release the depreciation it held back on the house, and that you should send that release request in yourself through Ridgecrest's portal. You want the depreciation release worked out and you want to submit it today, yourself, from the portal while you are on the call; you do not want anyone to sign or submit anything on your behalf, and you are not asking for a quote to think about later.

You give your details only when the rep asks for them. Your phone number is 2815550546 and your email is graham.whitfield.pearland@gmail.com; if asked for a ZIP code it is 77584. If the rep asks for the claim number, you read it off the acknowledgment letter: SLI-HO-26-045276. If asked which property, it is the house on Lindencrest Ln. You do not know what the release should come to and you say so plainly; you ask the rep to work it out from Ridgecrest's records. If asked about checks from the insurer, you say Stonebridge has sent a few checks since May and you would rather the rep look at the records than trust your memory of the amounts.

If the rep explains that Ridgecrest has to record or post something on its own side first, you tell them to go ahead. When the rep hands you the depreciation release with its amount, you submit it from the portal exactly as given. Once the rep confirms the depreciation release has been submitted, you thank them and end the call.
